This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement signal: its 2024 share of national LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases was 1.56% (Movilh regional table). Its recorded case trend follows the national one, which rose in 2025 to a record; a low share is not evidence of safety — most regions outside the two biggest rose that year.

There is no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division; its recorded profile comes from the shared national case table. National frame: 2025 produced a record 3,620 discrimination cases on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression (+27.1%; 23% of all cases in 24 years), and 2024 was the first regression since the return of democracy. Protective national framework (Gender Identity Law 21.120 in force 2019, same-sex marriage 2022, anti-discrimination law 21.220) sits against concrete 2025-26 rollback (PAIG excluded from the 2026 budget; health-ministry circular N8 restricting PAIG for minors; legislative initiative CEI-57) and administrative document friction from Registro Civil identification-system issuance failures (Comptroller Final Report 264/2025), which is directly relevant to a traveller whose documents must match presentation.

records.name: Gangwon
records.summary:
No province-specific law, ordinance or enforcement pattern targeting trans people is documented for Gangwon; the framework a visitor meets there is the national one: being trans is not criminalised, and the courts are steadily tightening what legal gender recognition may demand — a May 2024 ruling ended any surgical requirement for changing registered sex, and in July 2024 a court held that police telling a trans person to avoid public restrooms for a while infringed their rights, awarding damages after both instances found for the claimant and an appellate court calling comfortable restroom use a fundamental and universal human right.

The same sources describe both the promise and the limit of that judicial route: a 2021 damages award against an academy that barred a trans student from restrooms shows recourse exists, while a 2021 national survey of 591 trans respondents — 41% using wrong-gender facilities out of fear, 39% restricting food and drink to avoid restrooms, 36% skipping facilities altogether — shows everyday facility avoidance remains the norm. For a visitor, Gangwon's audited record offers legality, functioning courts and no local hostility machinery, with social friction around public restrooms documented nationally rather than locally.

records.name: Incheon
records.summary:
Incheon is documented by the audited record as a place with no specific local laws, ordinances or incident patterns concerning trans people; visitors stand under the national framework, which is favourable on paper and improving through litigation: trans status is not a crime; a May 2024 ruling confirmed surgery cannot be required to change registered legal sex; and in July 2024 a court held that police directing a transitioning person to avoid public restrooms infringed personal rights, an appellate court branding comfortable restroom use a fundamental and universal human right.

The same record supplies the practical counterweight: a 2021 national survey of trans respondents documents fear-driven restroom avoidance in striking majorities (41% had used a facility mismatching their identity; 36% forwent restroom use), and a 2021 award against a private academy that excluded a trans student shows courts intervene when facilities are denied. That mix — lawful status, an active and increasingly sympathetic judiciary, and socially contested facilities — is the documented experience of Incheon, no municipality-level initiative here being recorded either way.

records.name: Busan
records.summary:
Nothing in the audited sources documents a region-specific ordinance, incident series or enforcement pattern concerning trans people in this metropolitan area. The framework a visitor stands under is the national one: trans status is not criminalised; legal gender recognition exists but its medical prerequisites were struck down by a May 2024 court ruling; and in July 2024 a court held that police who advised a trans person to avoid public restrooms infringed personal rights, awarding damages after two instances ruled for the claimant, with the appellate court calling comfortable restroom use a fundamental and universal human right.

The same ruling's report adds the practical picture from national data: a 2021 human-rights commission survey of 591 trans respondents found fear-driven restroom avoidance routine (41% using mismatched facilities, 36% foregoing them), and a 2021 damages award went against an academy that barred a trans student from its restrooms. Audited evidence therefore supports legality, functioning judicial recourse and social ambivalence over facilities here; the audited record documents nothing about this city, favourable or unfavourable, that distinguishes it from that nationwide picture.

records.name: Ulsan
records.summary:
No audited source documents any local law, ordinance or enforcement practice regarding trans people in this industrial city; the national framework applies undiminished: trans status is lawful; legal gender recognition is available without surgical prerequisites after a May 2024 ruling; and the July 2024 judgment holding that police advice to avoid public restrooms was a rights infringement — damages awarded, the appellate court declaring comfortable restroom access a fundamental and universal human right — binds police practice as elsewhere in the country. The same case file records a 2021 national survey of trans respondents showing widespread fear-driven avoidance of public facilities, and a 2021 damages award to a student barred from an academy's restrooms.

Within the audited record, nothing in this city's own conduct — administration, policing or incident history — either worsens or improves that national baseline; the earlier suggestion that it shared the municipal-obstruction pattern documented for other cities was inference from party affiliation and survives no source. Its visitor-facing facts are therefore the framework plus the facility-avoidance survey, and no more.
